title: 90-degree pipe-bend STL geometry asset
overview: Defines the first parameterized curved-pipe STL asset: a 90-degree circular pipe bend with inlet and outlet straight extensions. The implementation includes Python and C++17 geometry generators, Geometry Library / Mesh Generation GUI controls, a generic region-aware Gmsh geometry handoff, and geometry-level verification. A registered production mesh Case, CGNS handoff, OneFLOW CFD run and physical validation remain future evidence.
principle: Separate centreline geometry, cross-section geometry, surface discretization and volume-mesh density. Preserve wall, inflow and outflow patch identity explicitly. The STL shell is a closed fluid-domain boundary: inlet/outlet disks close the shell but are not solid walls. The future meshing adapter must consume the STL and patch contract without depending on pipe-bend equations.
architecture: Parameter contract -> independent Python or C++17 swept-surface generator -> closed STL + geometry metadata -> Python wall/inflow/outflow patch STLs + oneflow.stl-surface-regions manifest -> Geometry Library / Generate STL Geometry GUI -> existing geometry-independent region-aware Gmsh converter -> MSH 4.1 -> future CGNS/OneFLOW CFD. The converter does not read pipe-bend equations, angle or bend radius. Python writes binary STL and checksum-bound manifests; C++ writes ASCII STL and a parameter/patch-count geometry report.

proves: The default 90-degree pipe-bend geometry is defined by a circular centreline arc joined tangentially to straight inlet and outlet segments.
The circular cross-section is transported continuously along the centreline frame.
The Python generator emits a watertight connected shell, a checksum-bound manifest and explicit wall/inflow/outflow triangle-index groups.
The C++17 generator emits an equivalent analytic pipe-bend surface using the same default geometric and discretization parameters.
The triangulated shell volume is checked against the analytic constant-area swept-volume formula.
Generated assets are intended for the user's .oneflow workspace rather than the source tree.
The Geometry Library and Generate STL Geometry GUI expose the 90-degree pipe bend and its analytic/discretization controls, generating output in the user's mesh-generation workspace.
The Python geometry generator exports separate wall, inflow and outflow STL patches plus a checksum-bound oneflow.stl-surface-regions manifest.

The existing region-aware generic STL-to-Gmsh converter produces a Gmsh geometry script that merges the three patch files, coheres shared nodes, constructs discrete geometry and assigns wall/inflow/outflow/fluid_domain Physical Groups without pipe-bend-specific equations.
The mesh-project importer preserves the region manifest and all three patch files when importing the generated STL.
The generic region-aware converter verifies that the three patch STL triangle geometries form an exact, non-overlapping partition of the closed STL, rather than relying only on triangle counts.
does_not_prove: The current pipe-bend geometry has been converted into a Gmsh tetrahedral volume mesh.
The pipe-bend mesh has been converted to CGNS or ingested by OneFLOW.
The C++ companion report has the same SHA-256 provenance fields as the Python manifest.
A production pipe-bend automatic_tetrahedra Case has been registered in the standard mesh Case catalog.
The resulting MSH 4.1 has been converted to CGNS or consumed by OneFLOW.
